impact.why: First measurement of leniency and rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline; silent coordination surviving report-based tools and the screen focal point are useful, but one stylised game.

execution.why: Pre-registration, scripted and known-effect controls, placebo, paraphrase and permutation tests are strong; 4 to 8 pools, a post-first-call extension and mixed pool counts weaken the headline.

presentation.why: Clear structure, findings up front, honest limitations; dense abstract, 4- and 8-pool numbers mixed without labels, and half of page 5 left empty.

summary_three_sentences: The report replays the Bigoni et al. (2012) cartel enforcement experiment with four LLM pricing agents under the same payoffs, regimes and matching, scoring them against the human results with a pre-registered rule. Without an authority all models form cartels and the Claude models hold them near the joint optimum; told fines, leniency and rewards remove explicit cartels, but three of four models keep silent supracompetitive prices, and a price screen lowers prices in three tested arms while Sonnet prices exactly at its threshold. Well supported are the controls, the laissez-faire cartels, the disappearance of explicit cartels and the silent prices above Nash; the human comparison is untested point estimates, and Haiku's three of seven reproduced results depend on the 8-pool extension and on the bootstrap rule for Result 3.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, Abstract, sentence starting 'Third, a pre-registered price screen'; page 6 to 7, Finding 3; Appendix B
top_fixes.change: Scope the screen claim to the three arms actually run (7.36 is Sonnet's no-channel price, not its silent price under prohibition), say whether agents were told the screen rule, and add the screen instruction text verbatim to Appendix B.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Third, a told price screen (false-positive rate at most 1.1 percent against scripted competitive players) lowered prices in all three arms tested, e.g. Sonnet without a channel from 7.36 to exactly 4.00, the highest allowed price, without a single penalty.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, Abstract, last sentence; page 5, paragraph 'Haiku reproduces three of seven'
top_fixes.change: Put the two caveats that the body already states into the headline: 8 pools came from amendment 4 after the first calls (4 pools give two of seven), and Result 3 fails the permutation test.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Under the primary pre-registered rule with 8 pool sessions, Haiku reproduces three of seven tested results of the human experiment (two of seven with the first 4 pools; Result 3 passes the bootstrap but not the permutation test, p 0.099).

top_fixes.where: Page 4 Finding 1 (formation 0.7159 vs 0.716); page 7 Table 4 caption and validity paragraph (placebo minus fine +0.275); page 5 empty lower half
top_fixes.change: Label every Haiku number with its pool count: the formation equality and the placebo difference use the first 4 pools, Table 4's Haiku fine baseline 5.52 uses 8 pools. Move Figure 1 up to fill page 5.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Over the first 4 pool sessions Haiku's formation rate equals the human one by a coincidence of rounding (0.7159 against 0.716); over all 8 it is higher (Figure 1).

contradictions.where: Page 4, Finding 1 vs Figure 1 panel 1 and Table 3 Result 1
contradictions.what: Text says Haiku formation equals human 0.716 (4-pool value); Figure 1 (8 pools) shows Haiku LF formation near 0.78, consistent with LF minus Fine +0.630.

contradictions.where: Page 7, Table 4 caption vs row 'Haiku 5.5, fine'
contradictions.what: Caption says 4 pool sessions per arm; baseline 5.52 and p 0.002 are 8-pool values (4-pool fine price is 5.59 in Table A1).

contradictions.where: Page 7, validity checks, placebo minus fine +0.275 vs Table 2
contradictions.what: 0.714 minus Table 2's fine incidence 0.401 is 0.313; +0.275 uses the 4-pool value 0.439 without saying so.

contradictions.where: Abstract and Finding 3 vs Section 5 'What this means for a competition authority'
contradictions.what: Abstract and Finding 3: Sonnet prices exactly at 4, the highest allowed price; Section 5: 'prices settle just below it'.

contradictions.where: Abstract, 'lowers these silent prices (Sonnet 7.36 to 4.00)' vs Table 2 and Table 4
contradictions.what: 7.36 is Sonnet's no-channel price; its silent prices under prohibition are 5.74 to 6.24, where the screen was never run.

contradictions.where: Section 5 ('a known threshold') and zero screen penalties vs Limitations 'Future work'
contradictions.what: Zero penalties imply agents were told the rule, yet future work proposes red-teaming 'against agents told its rule'; Appendix B omits the screen text.
Usage statement lists claude-opus-5-5 among models under test; Methods, tables and results name only four models.

contradictions.where: Finding 2 and Table 4, p 0.029 for 4 vs 4 pools vs Methods 'one-sided permutation test'
contradictions.what: For fully separated 4 vs 4 pools the exact one-sided minimum is 1/70 = 0.014; 0.029 = 2/70 suggests a two-sided test. Check.

contradictions.where: Page 1, Introduction, 'when they can talk (Fish et al., 2024; ...)'
contradictions.what: Fish et al. agents had no communication channel; Related Work itself says they collude autonomously.

overclaims.why: Screen tested only in two no-channel arms and Haiku fine; never on the silent prohibition prices of Sonnet, Qwen or Llama.

overclaims.sentence: remove explicit cartels from the agents far more than from people
overclaims.why: Untested point comparison; for Haiku under the fine incidence is 0.401 against 0.583, not far more.

overclaims.sentence: Haiku reproduces three of seven tested results
overclaims.why: Rests on the 8-pool extension added after first calls and on Result 3, which fails the registered permutation test.

overclaims.sentence: a false-positive rate of at most 1.1 percent
overclaims.why: Measured only on four scripted strategies, not on competitive LLM agents or realistic demand noise.

overclaims.sentence: the report rule acts in the humans' direction with a far larger effect
overclaims.why: Result 2 difference +0.543 vs human about +0.415; Haiku's leniency report rate 0.375 is below the human 0.507.

overclaims.sentence: a price floor that colluding agents will target
overclaims.why: One model in one no-channel arm; no evidence those Sonnet prices are collusion, and 'will' generalises beyond the data.

overclaims.sentence: a placebo arm and a contamination test validate the pipeline
overclaims.why: Haiku's fine effect fails paraphrase, Qwen fails the shifted grid, and the placebo shows wording drives part of the effect.

overclaims.sentence: in three of four models the price stays
overclaims.why: Sonnet's price drops 2.2 to 3.2 points from laissez-faire; it stays above Nash, not at its level.

red_lines.note: Mild and disclosed in the body: the abstract's three of seven omits that 4 pools give two and Result 3 fails the permutation test; Table 4 pairs an 8-pool baseline with 4-pool screen arms. Design credited to Bigoni; LLM use declared.
